notes:
Compatibility reports now know which emulator you actually used.

Nothing about how your games play changes in this update. What changes is the
community compatibility data: which emulator a report describes, and what
happens when you apply someone else's setup.

Three platforms can run on two different emulators: PS2 on ARMSX2 or AetherSX2,
DS on melonDS or DraStic, PSP on the RetroArch core or standalone PPSSPP. Until
now a report did not reliably say which one it used. DS reports made with
DraStic were filed as melonDS, and PSP reports made with standalone PPSSPP were
filed as the RetroArch core. On PS2, ratings from both emulators were pooled
into a single recommended setup, which could hand you settings that do not even
exist on the emulator you run.

Reports now record the emulator that really ran the game, community setups are
kept separate per emulator, and each report lists only that emulator's settings.

Applying a community setup now switches you to the emulator it was made on, so
you get the whole setup rather than one emulator's settings on another's engine.

Applying a setup no longer touches your overlays. Your stats overlay, your
emulator FPS overlay, and where they sit on screen are yours and stay put.

Most PS2 setups on record were made with AetherSX2, so applying one can switch
you to it. ARMSX2 is the default now, so this shifts as new reports arrive. DS
and PSP reports made before this update cannot say which emulator they used, so
applying one leaves your emulator alone rather than guessing.
